([[Seattle, Washington]]) * [[Federal Way High School|Federal Way]]
([[Federal Way, Washington]]) | college = * [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]] (2020–2021) * [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] (2021–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 17 | draft_team = [[Houston Rockets]] | career_start = 2022 | career_end = | years1 = {{nbay|2022|start}}–present | team1 = [[Houston Rockets]] | highlights = * [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] ({{nbay|2022|end}}) * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] Sixth Man of the Year (2022) * First-team All-SEC (2022) * [[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] All-Freshman Team (2021) }} '''Tari Jordan Eason''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|t|ɑː|r|i|_|ˈ|iː|s|ən}} {{respell|TAR|ee|_|EE|sən}};{{cite press release |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |date=October 24, 2023 |publisher=NBA |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |access-date=May 17, 2024 |author=}} born May 10, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati Bearcats]] and the [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU Tigers]]. Eason was selected 17th overall in the [[2022 NBA draft]] by the [[Houston Rockets]]. ==High school career== Eason started his high school career at [[Garfield High School (Seattle)|Garfield High School]] in [[Seattle, Washington]] under head coach [[Brandon Roy]], and played sparingly during his first two years.{{cite web |last=Evans |first=Jayda |title=Garfield's four-star prospect Tari Eason honors aunt with commitment to Cincinnati |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/garfields-four-star-prospect-tari-eason-honors-aunt-with-commitment-to-cincinnati/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=December 21, 2019}} For his junior season, he transferred to [[Federal Way High School]] in [[Federal Way, Washington]], where he played alongside top recruit [[Jaden McDaniels]].{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Lauren |title=Federal Way's Tari Eason has been to the Tacoma Dome, but hasn't played. With the Eagles, he could be the key to a 4A title |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article226792899.html |website=[[The News Tribune]] |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=February 28, 2019}} Eason returned to Garfield for his senior season as Roy came back following a one-year break. He led his team to a 3A state title, recording 21 points and 14 rebounds against [[Paolo Banchero]] and [[O'Dea High School]] in the final, and received tournament MVP.{{cite web |last=Buhler |first=Andy |title='We need you to be superman.' Tari Eason takes final bow in Garfield's dominant 3A state championship win over O'Dea |url=https://scorebooklive.com/washington/2020/03/07/we-need-you-to-be-superman-tari-eason-takes-final-bow-in-garfields-dominant-3a-state-championship-win-over-odea/ |website=SBLive |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=March 7, 2020}}{{cite web |last=Buhler |first=Andy |title=Watch: Garfield's Tari Eason reacts to winning 3A state title, tournament MVP |url=https://scorebooklive.com/washington/2020/03/08/watch-garfields-tari-eason-reacts-to-winning-3a-state-title-tournament-mvp/ |website=SBLive |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=March 8, 2020}} Eason averaged 23 points, eight rebounds, and three steals per game as a senior, and was named 3A Player of the Year.{{cite web |last=Springer |first=Scott |title=Highly-touted forward Tari Eason makes it official signing with UC basketball |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/university-of-cincinnati/2020/04/20/state-washington-standout-tari-eason-signs-cincinnati-basketball/5150092002/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=April 20, 2020}}{{cite web |title=Tari Eason |url=https://lsusports.net/sports/mb/roster/player/tari-eason/ |website=LSU Athletics |date=August 3, 2021 |access-date=November 28, 2021}} A four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]] over offers from [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]] and [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]].{{cite web |last=Evans |first=Corey |title=Cincinnati wins out with four-star forward Tari Eason |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/cincinnati-wins-out-with-four-star-forward-tari-eason |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=December 22, 2019}} ==College career== [[File:Tari Eason (cropped).jpg|thumb|Eason with [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]] in 2021]] On February 26, 2021, Eason posted a freshman season-high 20 points, 13 rebounds, and three blocks in a 91–71 win over [[2020–21 Tulane Green Wave men's basketball team|Tulane]].{{cite web |title=Davenport carries Cincinnati over Tulane 91–71 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401277854 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=February 26, 2021}} As a freshman at Cincinnati, he averaged 7.3 points, 5.9 rebounds, 1.3 blocks, and 1.2 steals per game, earning [[American Athletic Conference]] All-Freshman Team honors. For his sophomore season, Eason transferred to [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]].{{cite web |last=Jenkins |first=Keith |title=Former Cincinnati Bearcats All-AAC freshman forward Tari Eason transfers to LSU |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/university-of-cincinnati/2021/04/20/cincinnati-bearcats-basketball-tari-eason-transfers-lsu/7298528002/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=April 20, 2021}} He was named to the First Team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] as well as SEC Sixth Man of the Year.{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/33453309/men-basketball-all-sec-teams-awards-announced|title=Men's Basketball All-SEC Teams & Awards Announced |publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |access-date=March 8, 2022}} Eason averaged 16.9 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 1.9 steals per game.{{cite news |last=Bates |first=Greg |title=LSU's Tari Eason on his next step: 'I have no idea what the future holds' |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_3ce8ae9c-a736-11ec-8ea4-6bf52f512212.html |access-date=March 19, 2022 |work=[[The Advocate (Louisiana)|The Advocate]] |date=March 18, 2022}} On March 25, 2022, he declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite news |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=March 25, 2022 |title=Tari Eason to leave LSU Tigers basketball team, declare for NBA draft |work=[[ESPN]] |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33595126 |access-date=March 28, 2022}} == Professional career == === Houston Rockets (2022–present) === Eason was selected with the 17th overall pick by the [[Houston Rockets]] in the [[2022 NBA draft]]. Eason joined the Rockets' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] roster.{{Cite web |title=Houston Rockets 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612745/rockets |access-date=July 21, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} In his Summer League debut, Eason tallied 14 points and 13 rebounds in a 77–91 win over the [[2022–23 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]].{{Cite web |title=Houston Rockets vs Orlando Magic Jul 7, 2022 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/game/hou-vs-orl-1522200001/box-score |access-date=July 21, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} On July 18, 2022, Eason was named to the All-NBA Summer League First Team, averaging 17.2 points on 44.7 percent shooting from the field along with 1.8 steals and a block.{{Cite magazine |last=Davis |first=Coty |date=July 18, 2022 |title=Rockets Tari Eason Named All-NBA Summer League First Team |url=https://www.si.com/nba/rockets/news/houston-rookie-tari-eason-summer-league-first-team-honors |access-date=July 21, 2022 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en}} On October 2, Eason made his preseason debut, scoring 21 points off the bench in addition to securing ten rebounds, two assists, two steals, and one block in a 134–96 win against the [[2022–23 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web |title=San Antonio Spurs vs. Houston Rockets - NBA Box Score - October 2, 2022 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401474847 |access-date=October 4, 2022 |website=ESPN |language=en}} On October 19, 2022, he made his NBA debut with an 8-point and 7-rebound performance in a 117–107 loss to the [[2022–23 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web |title=Rockets vs. Hawks - NBA Box Score - October 19, 2022 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401468020 |access-date=October 20, 2022 |website=ESPN |language=en}} On February 1, 2023, Eason scored a career-high 20 points with 13 rebounds (12 of them being offensive rebounds) and three steals in only 19 minutes of play in a 112–106 win against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web |last=Quinn |first=Sam |date=February 2, 2023 |title=Rockets rookie Tari Eason posts one of the most bizarre box scores you will ever see in just 19 minutes |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/rockets-rookie-tari-eason-posts-one-of-the-most-bizarre-box-scores-you-will-ever-see-in-just-19-minutes/ |access-date=February 3, 2023 |website=CBS Sports}} On February 23, his hard foul on Vince Williams caused a season ending injury. On July 2, 2026, Eason re-signed on a five-year, $81.5 million contract to stay with the Rockets.{{Cite web |last=Wright |first=Michael C. |date=July 2, 2026 |title=Sources: Eason to return to Rockets on 5-year, $81.5M deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49253596/sources-eason-return-rockets-5-year-815m-deal |access-date=July 5, 2026 |website=ESPN}} == Personal life == Eason has three siblings.
